title_en: Cho Peaks Early, Argerich Holds Back
note_en: Cho already gets close to the maximum in the opening phrase, then eases back to catch a breath and climbs again. Argerich keeps the opening soft and builds in one go in the middle.

title_en: Gould Skips Repeats, Levit Keeps Them All
note_en: The same variation takes Gould 1:10 and Levit nearly 2 minutes. Gould skips both repeats; Levit observes every one and ends at the loudest point.

title_en: Soft Andsnes, Immediately Loud Hough
note_en: Andsnes begins very softly, while Hough comes in loud from the first note. Hough's version is 11 seconds shorter.

title_en: Straight-Building Perahia, Early-Peaking Ashkenazy
note_en: Perahia builds in one continuous rise with no pulling back and reaches the maximum late. Ashkenazy eases back once but still gets near the maximum earlier and sustains it for a long time.

title_en: Fast Argerich, Soft-Landing Andsnes
note_en: Argerich is 8 seconds shorter. Argerich runs loudly to the very end, while Andsnes sets the ending down at the softest level.

title_en: Loud at Once, Swelling and Releasing
note_en: Shishkin climbs to nearly the maximum in 10 seconds and holds it to the end. Lang Lang repeats a swell-and-release in every phrase.

title_en: Kissin Pours It Out, Lang Lang Builds Up
note_en: They shape the same 20-odd seconds in opposite ways. Kissin reaches maximum loudness as soon as the music starts and holds it to the end; Lang Lang saves strength and bursts out 5 seconds before the end.

title_en: A Lowered Back Half, One More Push at the End
note_en: Argerich sets the level a step lower after the first 10 seconds. Yeol Eum Son stays even, then rises to nearly the maximum again close to the end.

title_en: Same First Chord, Different Middle
note_en: Both strike the first chord at their loudest. Kleiber takes one big breath in the middle, while Thielemann eases back only a little and pushes on to the end.

title_en: Chung Sets Down Quickly, Kleiber Sinks Deep
note_en: Myung-Whun Chung drops to a soft level right after the climax. Kleiber sinks deepest in the second quiet passage, then bursts out of it.

title_en: Lang Lang Early, Kissin Late
note_en: Lang Lang hits the climax in the opening section and eases off from the middle. Kissin reaches nearly the maximum in 20 seconds and keeps an even level, playing loudest only after the main figure returns.

title_en: A Very Soft First Song, an Even First Song
note_en: Yunchan Lim keeps the first song very soft and sinks once more just before the middle. Shishkin doesn't drop the same spot much and carries on evenly.

title_en: A Growing Ending, a Shrinking Ending
note_en: Scheps builds toward the back and sings loudest just before the end. Buniatishvili reaches the climax in the early part, then repeatedly scales back and ends softly.

title_en: Loud Up Front, Loud at the Back
note_en: Horowitz plays loudest right from the start and eases off toward the end. Fray holds back until past the middle, then plays loudest.

title_en: Lang Lang Erupts Early, Ott Stays Even
note_en: Lang Lang plays loudest in the first half, then drops deep within 10 seconds. Ott never drops sharply and becomes loudest only in the latter part.

title_en: Cho Ends Softly, Thibaudet Erupts at the End
note_en: Cho passes the climax at the three-quarter mark and closes softly. Thibaudet builds the final return and rings out loudest at the very end.

title_en: After the Peak: Little Drop or Deep Drop
note_en: Both rise high in the middle but differ afterward. Perlman keeps the sound large, while Kyung Wha Chung pulls it down to the quietest level in 20 seconds.

title_en: Loud in the Middle, Held Back to the End
note_en: Yundi Li plays loudest in the middle and drops straight to the quietest level. Bruce Liu plays loudly for the first time only when a minute remains.

title_en: Loud at Once, Held Back to the End
note_en: Ozawa opens to nearly the maximum from the first tutti. Kleiber puts the first tutti a step lower and keeps things soft up to the climax near the end.

title_en: Loud from the Start, Loud Only at the End
note_en: Jansons reaches nearly the maximum in 18 seconds and holds a big sound to the end. Karajan sinks the middle deep and reaches the maximum only in the last few seconds.

title_en: Even Bavouzet, Deep-Sinking Cho
note_en: Bavouzet doesn't sink far even in the quiet places and reaches the maximum only at the climax. Cho reaches the maximum early, then drops straight to a very low level.

title_en: Fast Levit, Soft Pollini
note_en: Levit is over a minute shorter and keeps the level even. Pollini starts at the softest level and opens a wide gap between quiet and loud.

title_en: Ashkenazy Sets Down, Yundi Li Sustains
note_en: Both rise to their loudest a little past the middle. Afterward Ashkenazy sets the level down for a long stretch, while Yundi Li holds it up until just before the end.

title_en: Short Pressler, Soft Pires
note_en: Pressler is 41 seconds shorter. Pires plays the first note far more softly, while Pressler stays loud for a long stretch in the middle.

title_en: Sustaining Ashkenazy, Sparing Lugansky
note_en: The lengths are nearly the same. Ashkenazy rings the returning bells at maximum twice; Lugansky plays loudly only at a single climax.

title_en: Big Swings from Lang Lang, Even Paik
note_en: Lang Lang sings loudest a third of the way in and sinks deeply afterward. Paik runs 16 seconds longer and keeps things even.

title_en: Pollini Closes Softly, Lisitsa Loudest at the End
note_en: Pollini drops to the quietest level 40 seconds after the climax and leaves the ending soft too. Lisitsa pulls back 15 seconds before the end, then plays the final chord loudest.

title_en: Same Movement, One Minute Apart
note_en: Levit is 58 seconds shorter and holds loud playing longer. Gilels sinks deep once before the end, then rises again.

title_en: Pollini in the Middle, Rubinstein at the Very End
note_en: Pollini plays loudest two-thirds of the way through and keeps that level to the end. Rubinstein saves the loudest sound for the final chord.

title_en: Kaufmann Loud Early, Beczała Gathers for the End
note_en: Kaufmann already sings near the maximum at the first peak. Beczała keeps the first peak a step lower and gathers strength for the final cry.

title_en: A Climax Up Front, a Climax at the End
note_en: Pires is 34 seconds shorter and puts the loudest sound in the first half. Lang Lang pulls back once a minute before the end, then plays loudest 30 seconds from the finish.

title_en: All Four Alike, Loud Only at the End
note_en: Sobotka plays the opening call and the final chord at the same level. Marriner holds the opening down a step and gives the final chord the loudest sound.

title_en: Haochen Zhang Sustains, Yunchan Lim Sinks
note_en: Haochen Zhang holds loud playing for a long time and doesn't drop as deeply in the quiet passage. Yunchan Lim sinks the quiet passage before the end very deeply from early on.

title_en: A Re-Raised Ending, a Set-Down Ending
note_en: Both run about 9:25. Lisitsa pulls back deeply a minute before the end and closes loudly again; Sumino, after a later climax, sets the ending down softly.

title_en: The Original Cadenza and the Ossia
note_en: Yuja Wang begins the lighter original version softly and builds at the end, while Lang Lang pushes the heavier ossia loudly from the start.

title_en: Rubinstein Rises Early, Zimerman Steps Back First
note_en: Rubinstein leaves the quiet passage early and sustains a high level for a long time. Zimerman steps back once just before the climax, then rises in one go.

title_en: Kissin Sings Evenly, Cho Whispers
note_en: Kissin sings at a similar, even level from the opening, while Cho keeps the first 4 seconds very quiet and builds over 20 seconds.

title_en: Rubinstein Max at Once, Cho Enters Softly
note_en: Rubinstein enters at nearly the maximum from the first sound and finishes 24 seconds sooner. Cho enters at the softest level and sinks deeply and at length twice before the end.

title_en: The Exact Middle and the Final Chord
note_en: André puts the climax in the middle of the movement and sinks deeply once before the end. Herseth keeps the beginning and end even and gives the final chord the loudest sound.

title_en: Högner Dips Then Rises, Tuckwell Sustains
note_en: Högner steps back a level in the middle and rises again. Tuckwell is about 30 seconds shorter, sustains loud playing longer, and puts the climax on the final chord.

title_en: Same Length, Different Depth
note_en: Length and climax position are nearly the same. Karajan sinks the quiet passages deepest; Marriner sinks them less and sustains loud playing longer.

title_en: Loud at Once, Slowly Built
note_en: Järvi reaches nearly the maximum in a minute and pushes on loudly to the end. Nelsons starts softly, sinks once, then builds up at the end.

title_en: Peak at the End, Peak in the Middle
note_en: Gardiner puts the loudest sound in the closing rush, Bernstein in the middle. Bernstein takes the closing rush a step lower and closes more softly.

title_en: From the First Strike, From a Minute In
note_en: The St. Lawrence Quartet is already near the maximum on the first blow. The Emerson Quartet enters a step lower, holds back for nearly a minute, then drives hard.

title_en: Serkin Opens Loud, Cascioli Holds Back
note_en: Serkin plays the first melody loudly and already reaches nearly the maximum in the early part. Cascioli opens softly and holds back the maximum for over a minute.

title_en: Loud at Once, Built Up at the End
note_en: Pollini reaches nearly the maximum in 16 seconds and sustains loud playing for a long time. Lisitsa stays a step lower until the middle, then builds up over the last minute or so.
Melnikov plays the same movement in 7:38, Yuja Wang in 6:05. Melnikov closes at the softest level, while Yuja Wang drops less.

title_en: Mutter Holds Back Long, Bell Rises Early
note_en: Mutter opens the introduction at the softest level, stretches it past 30 seconds, then rises at once. Bell brings the orchestra up loud 8 seconds earlier than Mutter.

title_en: Buniatishvili Widens, Cho Narrows
note_en: Buniatishvili keeps the opening song very soft and opens the gap wide in the minor-key passage. Cho enters loudly from the start and narrows that difference.

title_en: Pollini Front-Loads, Lupu Saves It for the End
note_en: Pollini is loudest at the first answer and stays even to the end. Lupu lowers the middle a step, then rises to the loudest level at the very end.

title_en: In 20 Seconds, After Over a Minute
note_en: Karajan reaches nearly the maximum in 20 seconds and sustains loud playing for a long time. Muti lingers softly for a long while and reaches nearly the maximum only 20 seconds before the end.

title_en: Abbado's Second Louder, Chailly's First Louder
note_en: Abbado blasts out the second fanfare louder than the first. Chailly's first fanfare is the loudest, and the passage runs 16 seconds shorter.

title_en: A Soft Bassoon, a Loud Bassoon
note_en: Gergiev brings in the bassoon very softly and builds little by little for over a minute. Mehta opens with the bassoon already loud, keeps the level for a while, then raises it at the end.

title_en: Climax in the First Passage, Climax at the End
note_en: Lang Lang is already loudest in the first fast passage. Trifonov scales back as far as possible later on, then rises to the loudest level in 24 seconds.

title_en: Lim After the Peak, Kissin Before the Peak
note_en: Lim plays 41 seconds longer and drops to the softest level after the peak. Kissin is near the maximum even before the climax and sustains loud playing for a long time.

title_en: Soft Chailly, Litton's Late Peak
note_en: Chailly opens at the softest level and rises to the loudest point in the front part of the middle. Litton starts loud and puts the loudest sound toward the back.

title_en: Ciccolini Builds to the End, Haskil Peaks Mid-Way
note_en: Haskil is about 1:40 shorter. Ciccolini opens softly and plays the final chord loudest, while Haskil plays loudest in a middle variation.

title_en: Bernstein Raises Early, Thibaudet Holds Back
note_en: Bernstein raises the level a step from the middle on and builds further at the end. Thibaudet keeps the middle low too and rises in one go at the end.

title_en: Loud from the Start, Held Back to the End
note_en: Rubinstein enters at nearly the maximum from the first sound and sustains it to the end. Giltburg drags the middle at a low level and reaches nearly the maximum only 40 seconds before the end.

title_en: Big Swings from Buniatishvili, Even Zimerman
note_en: The lengths are nearly the same. Buniatishvili opens at the softest level and swings widely; Zimerman reaches nearly the maximum early and keeps things even.

title_en: Muti Stays Low, Masur Sinks Deep
note_en: Muti keeps the first minute low and piles it up in the last 20 seconds. Masur sinks deepest early on, then soon builds loudly.

title_en: Bernstein Holds Back, Mehta Raises Early
note_en: Bernstein holds back for the first 30 seconds and gets loud only after nearly a minute. Mehta enters loudly from the start and sustains loud playing for a long time.

title_en: Maximum at Once, Saved for Later
note_en: Dutoit pushes at nearly the maximum from the first sound to the end. Abbado keeps the first half a step lower, then drives upward in the later part.

title_en: Kissin at the Back, Perahia at the Start
note_en: Perahia plays the first descending chord loudest. Kissin sinks the theme deeply and plays loudest in the big passage later on.

title_en: Tsujii Sustains, Cho Rises at the End
note_en: Tsujii climbs once and keeps a loud level to the end. Cho sinks deeply once, then rises to the loudest level in the last few seconds.

title_en: Argerich Sustains, Ott Sinks
note_en: Argerich holds the first loud passage for a long time and drops less deeply than Ott. Ott reaches the maximum early, then sinks deeply and for a long time later.

title_en: Fast Karajan, Slow Bernstein
note_en: The same passage takes Karajan 1:15 and Bernstein 1:43. Karajan lays down the opening at the softest level; Bernstein starts louder.

title_en: Abbado Small, Karajan Early
note_en: Abbado keeps nearly the first minute very small, then stands up loudly all at once. Karajan raises the level little by little from the opening and gets near the maximum about 13 seconds earlier.

title_en: Same Quiet Passage, Different Depth
note_en: In the same quiet passage Abbado sinks the lowest of the three. Marriner descends the least and also closes nearly at the maximum.

title_en: Quiet Mutter, Bell Loud for Long
note_en: Mutter starts at the softest level and sinks deeply even after the climax. Bell drops only slightly after the climax and sustains loud playing the longest.

title_en: Same Song, Different Peak Position
note_en: Ottensamer stretches the song out and puts the climax toward the back. Meyer opens softly, sings loudest early on, then keeps the loud passage short.

title_en: Loud Up Front, Loud Only at the End
note_en: Maisky starts building after 20 seconds and is already loud in the early part. Yo-Yo Ma stays soft for over a minute and puts the climax right before the end.

title_en: Bernstein Opens Loud, Karajan Opens Soft
note_en: Karajan brings out the first motif the softest of the three and is loudest in the middle. Bernstein plays the first motif loudly and is loudest at the end.

title_en: Same Passage, 23 Seconds Apart
note_en: Davis takes 1:18 for the passage and Bernstein 1:41. Davis keeps the level even, while Bernstein sinks deeply before the climax.

title_en: Keeping the Back Loud or Thinning It Out
note_en: Both are loudest within the first 15 seconds. After that, Barenboim leaves the later sound loud, while Marriner thins it out to very soft.

title_en: Fast Marriner, Slow Bernstein
note_en: Marriner takes the same introduction in 1:38 and Bernstein in 2:26. Marriner re-establishes loud playing a few times; Bernstein stays soft after the first minute.

title_en: Fast Karajan, Böhm Saves It for the End
note_en: Böhm is 13 seconds longer. Karajan is loudest at the early high point; Böhm holds that point back a step and rises to the loudest level at the end.

title_en: Shallow Bernstein, Deep Fischer
note_en: Bernstein keeps the quiet passages shallow and climbs back close to the level of the first chord by the end. Fischer sinks the same passage deeper and for longer.

title_en: From the Very Start, Only After a Minute
note_en: Thibaudet plays at nearly the maximum from the very opening, which the timpani begin. Rogé builds a step at a time and plays loudest only after more than a minute.

title_en: Soft Ashkenazy, Early-Loud Lang Lang
note_en: Ashkenazy keeps the introduction at the softest level and reaches the maximum only within the last 10 seconds. Lang Lang is less soft from the introduction on and gets near the maximum over 20 seconds earlier.

title_en: Soft Timpani, Loud Timpani
note_en: Mutter opens the same five drumbeats at the softest level, Hahn at the loudest. Hahn passes through this stretch 9 seconds faster than Mutter.

title_en: An Early Climax, a Late Climax
note_en: Kang peaks early and drops to the quietest level in 9 seconds. Mutter sinks deeply once and reaches the climax 24 seconds later.

title_en: From the First Chord, After the Barrage
note_en: Pollini hammers the first chord at the maximum. Lang Lang saves the first chord and rises to the maximum only after the run of repeated blows.

title_en: Smaller Drop, Deeper Drop
note_en: Yundi Li doesn't reduce the level much even in the quiet theme. Perahia drops deep every time the theme returns.

title_en: Even Borodin, Wide-Ranging Emerson
note_en: The Borodin Quartet keeps the difference in level smallest and puts the loudest sound late. The Emerson Quartet drops to a very soft level, then rises to the maximum in 12 seconds.

title_en: Bronfman Rises Early, Schiff Rises at the End
note_en: Both come down once in the middle. Bronfman drops only slightly, then soon climbs to the loudest level; Schiff sinks deeply and rises only at the end.

title_en: Even Chailly, Early-Rising Abbado
note_en: Chailly keeps the level even from the first sound and gets loud only near the end. Abbado opens softly but reaches nearly the maximum in the middle first.

title_en: Early-Building Haitink, Hushed Karajan
note_en: Haitink reaches nearly the maximum in a minute and sustains it for a long time. Karajan opens at the softest level and reaches nearly the maximum only just before the climax.

title_en: First Passage or the End?
note_en: Karajan brings the sound back up to its loudest at the end after having lowered it. Abbado is loudest in the first passage and doesn't raise the ending as much.

title_en: Barenboim Arrives Early, Previn Only at the End
note_en: Barenboim gets nearly to the maximum in under a minute. Previn keeps the first two peaks a step lower and gets nearly to the maximum only at the end.

title_en: Previn Loud at Once, Denk Builds Softly
note_en: Previn reaches nearly the maximum in 20 seconds and keeps things even. Denk opens the cello at the softest level, steps back once, then builds for nearly a minute.

title_en: Argerich Sinks, Pires Raises Again
note_en: Both play the first chord at their loudest. Argerich sinks the second theme deepest and longest, while Pires sinks once and raises it loudly again at the end.

title_en: A Shallow Reduction, Almost Silence
note_en: Karajan is 18 seconds shorter and reduces the middle only slightly. Gergiev sinks the same spot almost to silence.

title_en: Muti Loud at Once, Relaxed Chailly
note_en: Muti enters at nearly the maximum on the first theme and reaches the climax earliest. Chailly runs about 20 seconds longer and puts the climax right in the middle.

title_en: Previn First, Karajan Longer
note_en: Previn reaches nearly the maximum in under a minute. Karajan is 9 seconds shorter and keeps pushing loudly to the end after the climax.

title_en: Davis Softly In and Out, Frühbeck de Burgos Clear
note_en: Davis runs about a minute longer. Davis puts the beginning and end at the softest level, while Frühbeck de Burgos pushes loudly from start to finish.

title_en: Reaching Early, Rising Late
note_en: Fischer-Dieskau reaches nearly the maximum early and leaves the ending loud too. Terfel postpones the loudest sound until near the end and leaves the finish very soft.

title_en: One Late Leap, Early Step-by-Step
note_en: Dutoit keeps the middle low, then rises to the maximum in 8 seconds at the end. Ozawa starts getting louder 15 seconds earlier and builds step by step.

title_en: Once Early, Once at the End
note_en: Gergiev is 28 seconds shorter than Haitink and is already near the maximum early on. Haitink sinks deeply in the middle and rises to the maximum only once, at the end.

title_en: Bernstein Comes Down After the Peak, Karajan Sustains
note_en: Both are loudest in the exact middle. Bernstein then comes down a step and ends softly, while Karajan stays at nearly that level to the end.

title_en: Dutoit at the Very End, Karajan a Minute Earlier
note_en: Dutoit keeps the middle soft and becomes loudest at the very end. Karajan raises the middle loudly too and becomes loudest about a minute before the end.

title_en: Muti Pauses Briefly, Chung Lingers
note_en: Muti passes through the hushed passage between the two outcries in 39 seconds. Myung-Whun Chung stretches the same passage to nearly a minute and plays the first outcry louder.

title_en: Same Oboe, Different Level
note_en: Bernstein brings out the first oboe song loudly and also runs shorter. Tilson Thomas keeps the first song soft and gets nearly to the maximum earlier.

title_en: Ozawa Up Front, Haitink at the End
note_en: Ozawa puts the loudest sound in the early tutti. Haitink sinks the middle deeply and plays loudest at the end.

title_en: A Deep Middle, an Even Middle
note_en: Dutoit eases off right after the first chord and sinks the middle deeply. Bernstein doesn't reduce much and pushes on at the same level.

title_en: Maximum at Once, Held Back to the End
note_en: Previn reaches nearly the maximum 8 seconds after the fanfare and sustains it for a long time. Dutoit reduces the middle to a small level and gets nearly to the maximum only when the march returns.

title_en: Softer Hahn/Marriner, Softest Mutter/Karajan
note_en: Hahn and Marriner bring out the first theme less softly and sustain the big passage for a long time. Mutter and Karajan set the first theme at the softest level and open the gap wide.

title_en: Short Barenboim, Long Mehta
note_en: Mehta is 33 seconds longer. Barenboim lets the sound down the most after the climax, while Mehta starts at the softest level and keeps it big to the end.

title_en: Loud-Opening Davis, Softly Drawn-Out Tilson Thomas
note_en: Both are loudest near the end. Davis plays the first sound loudest, while Tilson Thomas stretches out the opening section at the softest level.

title_en: Nézet-Séguin Holds Back, Bernstein Sustains
note_en: Nézet-Séguin holds back nearly the maximum until 30 seconds before the end. Bernstein reaches nearly the maximum from the middle and sustains it to the end.

title_en: Abbado Opens Softly, Nelsons Sustains
note_en: Abbado brings out the first chorale at the softest level and places the climax 13 seconds before the end. Nelsons sustains loud playing the longest and becomes loudest at the very end.

title_en: Miklósa Sinks, Gruberová Sustains
note_en: Both are loudest about 20 seconds before the end. Before that, Miklósa sinks for a long stretch, while Gruberová drops only slightly.

title_en: Flórez Presses Down, Beczała Cries Out Early
note_en: Flórez keeps most of the song pressed down softly and reaches the maximum only at the very end. Beczała already cries out at nearly the maximum at the end of the first verse.

title_en: Karajan Opens Loud, Pappano Opens Soft
note_en: Karajan enters loudly from the first fanfare and stays even to the end. Pappano starts softly and begins to get louder only 12 seconds before the end.

title_en: Solti Opens Softly, Muti Opens Loud
note_en: Solti opens the prelude softly and raises it a step at a time toward the end. Muti opens the prelude loudly, takes one more breath before the final chord, and then rises.

title_en: Bernstein on the First Chord, Karajan Just Before the End
note_en: Bernstein is loudest on the first chord and leaves the closing section loud too. Karajan rises to the loudest level just before the closing section, then sinks the deepest.

title_en: Abbado Gathers for the End, Rattle Loud Twice
note_en: Rattle is about a minute shorter. Abbado sings loudly only at the final surge, while Rattle sings as loudly in the middle as at the end.

title_en: A Less Soft Start, a Very Soft Start
note_en: Karajan starts less softly than the other two from the first sound and sustains loud playing for a long time. Davis starts very softly and rises to the maximum in 6 seconds.

title_en: 45 Seconds and 6 Seconds
note_en: Bernstein reaches nearly the maximum in 6 seconds and blasts out both rising points at the same level. Noseda starts at the softest level and takes about 45 seconds to reach the maximum.

title_en: Even Solti, Deep-Sinking Tilson Thomas
note_en: Solti doesn't sink far between the chords or in the middle. Tilson Thomas sinks the middle as deeply as at the start, then rises again.

title_en: Solti at the Opening, Nelsons Toward the End
note_en: Solti plays loudest from the first beat through the 9-second mark. Nelsons opens a step lower and puts the loudest sound toward the end.

title_en: Let There Be Light, 30 Seconds Apart
note_en: Solti reaches the burst of light early, dropping the sound very low just before it. Bernstein opens even more quietly and takes over 30 seconds longer.

title_en: Same Pace, Different Last Verse
note_en: The two performances keep nearly the same pace up to the passage about the wind. Fischer-Dieskau sings the last verse loudly again, while Goerne sets it down little by little to the end.

title_en: Gerhaher's Soft Prelude, Goerne Holds Back the First Verse
note_en: Gerhaher opens the prelude at the softest level and sings the first verse at nearly the maximum. Goerne keeps the first verse a step lower and gathers strength for the second.

title_en: Filling Quickly, Reaching Late
note_en: Solti fills the sound in under half a minute and pushes on at that level. Dutoit reaches the peak only after building for nearly a minute, and cuts the loud passages short.

title_en: Fast Jansons, Long-Hushed Karajan
note_en: Jansons passes through in 1:37 and plays loudly from the first phrases. Karajan runs 24 seconds longer and sinks deepest between phrases.

title_en: Even Katsaris, Growing Barenboim
note_en: Katsaris runs at nearly the same level through 49 seconds. Barenboim runs 8 seconds longer, starts softly, and builds toward the end.

title_en: Münchinger's Late Peak, Zinman's Early Peak
note_en: Zinman reaches the peak 26 seconds in and sustains loud playing the longest. Münchinger runs 16 seconds longer and puts the climax toward the back.

title_en: Maximum in the Middle, Only at the Last Chord
note_en: Schneider reaches nearly the maximum already in the middle and sustains it for a long time. Willens does not get near the maximum until the last chord and stays even.

title_en: Opening Loud, Opening Soft
note_en: Kasarova is 40 seconds longer. Von Stade starts loudly and becomes loudest near the end, while Kasarova opens softly and becomes loudest in the exact middle.

title_en: Holding Back to the Close, Big from the Start
note_en: Abbado holds the level back throughout the main body and rings out loudest on the closing chord. Bernstein is already loudest in the early part and sustains loud playing the longest.

title_en: Davis Opens Softly, Ozawa Opens Loud
note_en: Davis plays the first timpani at the softest level and has the widest gap in level. Ozawa starts less softly and sustains loud playing the longest.

title_en: Even Brunner, Meyer Building Toward the End
note_en: Brunner keeps the level even and puts the loudest sound in the early part. Meyer builds up again after a quiet spot and rings out loudest toward the end.

title_en: Christ Sustains, Malý Sinks
note_en: Both are loudest at the first tutti. Christ rises to that level twice more later, while Malý sinks the middle deeply.

title_en: Rattle at the Crescendo Peak, Karajan at the Very End
note_en: Karajan is 36 seconds shorter. Rattle is loudest at the top of the crescendo, while Karajan sinks deeper and is loudest at the very end.

title_en: Vishnevskaya in the Second Verse, Sukmanova in the First
note_en: Vishnevskaya sings loudest in the second verse and closes very softly. Sukmanova is loudest in the first verse and sings the second nearly as loudly.

title_en: Bernstein Rises Early, Dutoit at the End
note_en: Bernstein reaches nearly the maximum over 2 minutes earlier than Dutoit. Dutoit rings out loudest only a few seconds before the end, and the whole performance is 54 seconds longer.

title_en: Karajan Builds, Gergiev Sinks
note_en: Both open the Sultan's theme at their loudest. Karajan builds steadily after the middle, while Gergiev sinks the middle to the lowest level and raises it late.

title_en: Davis Rises in the Middle, Muti Holds Back
note_en: At the same spot Davis rises to nearly the maximum and Muti stops just below it. Muti gets nearly to the maximum only just before the last chord.

title_en: Reiner Strikes at Once, Maazel Holds Back
note_en: Reiner strikes at nearly the maximum from the first sound and plays the dawn less softly. Maazel holds back for about 2 minutes before raising the level, and sinks the dawn very softly.

title_en: Karajan Sustains, Jansons Cuts Short
note_en: Karajan gets nearly to the maximum early and carries on to the climax for a long time. Jansons gets nearly to the maximum only just before the climax.

title_en: A Climax Within 30 Seconds, a Climax in the Exact Middle
note_en: The Takács Quartet reaches the climax within 30 seconds and sustains loud playing the longest. The Alban Berg Quartett opens at the softest level and reaches the climax only in the exact middle.

title_en: Deep-Sinking Solti, Short Karajan
note_en: Solti stretches the passage after the chords out at the softest level. Karajan is 17 seconds shorter and passes through with quiet spots that sink less.

title_en: Same Piece, 24 Seconds Apart
note_en: Firkušný is 24 seconds shorter. Lympany keeps a similar, even level, while Firkušný sets the beginning and end softly and rises loudly once in the middle.

title_en: Same Crescendo, Different Start
note_en: Böhm starts getting louder earlier than the other two and builds for about 20 seconds. Chailly starts latest and rises in one go within about 15 seconds.

title_en: Polyphony at the Front, Monteverdi at the Back
note_en: Polyphony sings loudest in the early part and soon sinks. The Monteverdi Choir runs 25 seconds longer, lowers the middle to the smallest level, and is loudest toward the back.

title_en: Tilson Thomas Stretches, Ozawa Cuts Short
note_en: Tilson Thomas holds nearly the maximum for almost 20 seconds before reaching the climax. Ozawa strikes the climax in one go and soon sets it down.

title_en: Abbado Surges Late, Solti Builds Early
note_en: Abbado sinks the middle deepest and surges in the last 20 seconds or so. Solti pushes the opening loudest and also starts building again earliest.

title_en: Tilson Thomas Rises Early, Haitink Holds Back
note_en: Tilson Thomas reaches nearly the maximum in 36 seconds and sustains it for a long time. Haitink opens on the softest pedal tone, holds back for over a minute, then rises.

title_en: Loud at Once, Held Back Over 30 Seconds
note_en: Dudamel enters at nearly the maximum on the first outcry and pushes evenly to the end. Abbado opens a step lower and reaches the maximum only after more than 30 seconds.

title_en: Maximum at the Opening, Maximum at the End
note_en: Solti blasts loudest at the horn signal, while Bernstein blasts loudest in the last few seconds. Both lower the middle a step in between.

title_en: Maazel Up Front, Karajan at the Back
note_en: Maazel strikes the climax in the first big passage of the introduction and doesn't raise it as much later. Karajan opens at the softest level and reaches the climax in the later big passage.

title_en: Very Soft Capuçon, Clear Mutter
note_en: Capuçon keeps the opening very soft and runs about 10 seconds longer than Mutter. Mutter plays loudly from the first note and carries that strength to the end.

title_en: Barenboim at the Back, Dutoit Up Front
note_en: Dutoit sings loudest within a minute and gets nearly to the maximum twice more afterward. Barenboim keeps the early part soft and sings loudest in the later part.

title_en: Short Devieilhe, Long Fleming
note_en: Devieilhe sings it in 2:40 and goes to nearly the maximum from the first line. Fleming stretches it 40 seconds longer and sings loudest only after the middle.

title_en: Ormandy Doesn't Reduce, Marriner Sinks
note_en: Ormandy is 49 seconds longer. Ormandy carries on through the middle without reducing, while Marriner sinks to the smallest level within a big passage and raises it again.

title_en: Climax Up Front, Climax in the Middle
note_en: Isserlis sings loudest within the first melody. Yo-Yo Ma flows through about 15 seconds shorter and puts the loudest singing at the end of the middle section.

title_en: Even Pressler, Orkis Lowering the Back
note_en: Pressler keeps the level even after the climax and reaches the maximum again near the end. Orkis comes down a step after the climax and plays the back part lowest.

title_en: Climax Early, Climax Late
note_en: Bernstein is about 10 seconds shorter than the other two and puts the climax in the early part. Dutoit plays loudest in the later part and sets the ending down very softly.

title_en: An Early Peak and a Late Peak
note_en: Shelley rises to the loudest level right at the opening and sustains loud playing for a long time. Kanneh-Mason puts the loudest sound just before a deep sinking.

title_en: Same Back Half, Different Depth
note_en: In the same quiet passage in the back part, Kang doesn't reduce the level much. Janssen sinks very deeply there and then rises again.

title_en: From the First Chord, Only After a Minute
note_en: Midori sounds the first chord loudest. Perlman first gets near the maximum only in the surging passage around the one-minute mark, then drops the deepest afterward.

title_en: How Deep It Comes Down After the Peak
note_en: Both sink the middle deeply and rise loudly. Accardo comes down sharply soon after the peak, while Baráti doesn't come down as far.

title_en: The Depth of the Middle Differs
note_en: Thibaudet sinks the middle only slightly and rolls along evenly. Cho runs 25 seconds longer and sinks the middle deepest and longest.

title_en: Karajan Stretches, Dutoit Soars Early
note_en: Karajan takes 2 minutes, staying soft for over a minute before soaring. Dutoit passes through in 1:37 and starts getting louder about 10 seconds earlier.

title_en: Shallow Haitink, Deep Abbado
note_en: Abbado is 15 seconds shorter. Haitink sinks the early part the shallowest, while Abbado sinks the deepest and keeps things soft until the middle.

title_en: Deep Shelley, Even Lisiecki
note_en: Shelley sinks the middle song the deepest and becomes loudest at the returning march. Lisiecki carries the middle on loudly too.

title_en: Yuja Wang Stretches the Middle, Lang Lang Ends Early
note_en: Yuja Wang comes down only slightly even before the climax and carries the middle on loudly. Lang Lang reaches the climax 18 seconds earlier and closes the ending at the softest level.

title_en: Rogé Sustains, Argerich Sinks
note_en: Rogé sustains loud playing for a long time and sinks the later part less. Argerich sinks the relaxed passage to the smallest level.

title_en: The Last 5 Seconds and the Exact Middle
note_en: Abbado reaches nearly the maximum in the exact middle and sustains it to the end. Solti holds back until 5 seconds from the end, then rises in one go.

title_en: Soft Thibaudet, Even Liu
note_en: Thibaudet brings out the first melody very softly and builds it up big. Liu brings out the first melody loudly and flows most evenly.

title_en: Deep Muti, Shallow Levine
note_en: Both are loudest at the end of the last verse. Muti sinks deeply each time a verse begins anew, while Levine comes down only a little.

title_en: Rogé at 5 Minutes, Ciccolini at 6
note_en: Ciccolini is a minute longer. Rogé opens at the softest level and builds big, while Ciccolini keeps the most even level of the three.

title_en: Muti at the First Cry, Levine at the Last
note_en: Muti is loudest at the first outcry and sinks deeply right after. Levine builds toward the end and rings out loudest at the last outcry.

title_en: Climax After the Pause, Climax Before the Pause
note_en: Kyung Wha Chung makes a deep pause in the middle, builds again, and plays loudest at the end. Accardo plays loudest just before the pause and sinks to the deepest level at once.

title_en: Even Aimard, Deep-Sinking Denk
note_en: Aimard carries the beginning and end evenly and is loudest in the middle. Denk rises to the loudest level in 9 seconds, then sinks the middle deepest.
Ozawa passes through the same passage in 2:52, Tilson Thomas in 3:31. Ozawa starts getting louder early, while Tilson Thomas rises in two stages.

title_en: Short Jansons, Long Noseda
note_en: Noseda is 35 seconds longer. Noseda holds the quiet passage the softest and for the longest, while Jansons passes through it quickly and rises.

title_en: Maximum at the End, Maximum at the Start
note_en: Ormandy rings out loudest at the first tutti, while Previn rises to the loudest level at the last tutti, where everything gathers again.

title_en: Peak Up Front, Peak at the End
note_en: Mørk puts the loudest sound in the early part, Gerhardt at the end. Gerhardt presses the moment just before it down very small to heighten the contrast.

title_en: Early-Reaching LaSalle, Deep-Sinking Emerson
note_en: The LaSalle Quartet reaches nearly the maximum within 30 seconds and reduces the middle less than the Emerson Quartet. The Emerson runs about 10 seconds longer and sinks the middle to the smallest level.

title_en: Perlman in the Middle, Capuçon at the Very End
note_en: Perlman rises to the loudest level in the middle, then sinks deeply. Capuçon builds little by little and rises loudest at the very end.

title_en: Tilson Thomas Sustains, Masur Strikes Briefly
note_en: Tilson Thomas reaches nearly the maximum twice in the big passage and sustains it for a long time. Masur strikes the top once, briefly, then comes down to a very soft level.

title_en: Emerson Opens the Gap, Italiano Stays Narrow
note_en: The Quartetto Italiano runs 23 seconds longer and keeps the whispers less small. The Emerson Quartet strikes the first gesture hard, then drops straight to the smallest level.

title_en: Boulez Ends Softly, Karajan Sustains
note_en: Boulez keeps the loud passages short and sets the ending down the softest. Karajan sustains loud playing the longest and closes less softly.

title_en: Loriod Big from the Start, Thibaudet Holds Back
note_en: Loriod opens at nearly the maximum from the very beginning and sustains loud playing the longest. Thibaudet reaches that level for the first time only a few seconds before the end.

title_en: Even Fröst, Shaham Opening Softly
note_en: Fröst enters loudly from the first sound and stays even to the end. Shaham opens very softly and raises the level little by little toward the end.

title_en: Rozhdestvensky Sinks, Ormandy Sustains
note_en: In the middle song, Rozhdestvensky sinks the level the deepest, while Ormandy lowers it only slightly.

title_en: Ricci at the First Tutti, Mordkovitch Rising Later
note_en: Ricci is loudest at the first tutti. Mordkovitch sinks deeply after the first tutti, builds again, and rises to the loudest level.

title_en: Järvi Sets Down, Black Pushes to the End
note_en: Järvi plays loudest in the last big passage, then sets the ending down. Black pushes to the end and plays the final chord loudest.

title_en: Cello Loud at Once, Trumpet Builds Up
note_en: The cello version enters loudly from the start and barely changes the level over its 3 minutes. The trumpet version opens softly and builds for over 4 minutes.

title_en: Cello and Piano, Violin and String Orchestra
note_en: The cello version rises early, steps back once, and rises again. The violin version runs about a minute longer and reaches nearly the maximum only once, late.

title_en: One Guitar, Quartet and Orchestra
note_en: The guitar plays the piece in 4:41, the quartet-and-orchestra version in 7:07. The orchestral version sustains loud playing for a long time, while the guitar keeps an even level.

title_en: Long Domingo, Early-Rising Carreras
note_en: Domingo sings 47 seconds longer and reaches nearly the maximum only 40 seconds before the end. Carreras gets there about a minute and a half earlier.

title_en: Tiempo at the Front, Steinbacher at the End
note_en: The two-piano version peaks about a quarter of the way in, the violin version near the end. The lengths also differ by about two and a half minutes.

title_en: One Voice, a Whole Orchestra
note_en: The voice sings the same melody in under 5 minutes, the orchestra takes 7. The voice diminishes with every breath, while the orchestra swings widely each time the instruments change.

title_en: Peak in the Middle, Peak Only at the End
note_en: Gheorghiu sings at nearly the maximum as soon as the quiet middle passage ends. Gruberová holds that level back until 16 seconds before the end.

title_en: Chailly Surges at the End, Chung Builds Long
note_en: Chung is 17 seconds longer. Chailly keeps the middle low and raises it loudly over the last 30 seconds; Chung builds to a big sound and goes up one more step at the end.

title_en: Zimerman Builds Long, Trifonov Pushes to the End
note_en: From a very soft first chord, Zimerman builds the bell sound for over 30 seconds. Trifonov starts less softly, moves on to the theme early, and carries on loudly to the end.

title_en: Perahia Connects Quickly, Zimerman Sinks Deep
note_en: Perahia is 10 seconds shorter. Perahia keeps the quiet passages shallow and carries the hymn on, while Zimerman sinks much deeper.

title_en: Solti Loud at First Fortissimo, Karajan at Second Theme
note_en: Solti blasts out loudest at the first fortissimo at the end of the fugato. Karajan holds that passage back and rises loudest at the second theme.

title_en: Relaxed Fabbricini, Short Cotrubaș
note_en: The same scene takes Fabbricini 2:40 and Cotrubaș 2:06. Fabbricini presses the early dialogue down softly, while Cotrubaș rises loudly once in the middle of the dialogue.

title_en: Solti Holds to the End, Haitink Steps Down
note_en: Solti keeps the level of the first sound to the end and rises to that level again in the last big passage. Haitink steps down a level after the first sound and carries on beneath it.

title_en: Karajan Lowers Deep, Solti Lowers Less
note_en: Karajan lowers the opening and the passage leading into the recapitulation to a very soft level. Solti lowers the quiet passages less and plays the loudest sound in the exposition.

title_en: Loud Again on the Repeat, a Step Softer Each Time
note_en: Schiff is 21 seconds shorter. Schiff plays loudest in the repeat, while Hewitt plays each repetition of the same half one step softer.

title_en: Bernstein Lowers Less, Davis Lowers Deep
note_en: Davis is 22 seconds longer. When the women's chorus enters, Bernstein lowers the level less, while Davis lowers it far deeper and sets it against the outcry.

title_en: Sokolov Ends Loud, Hewitt Ends Soft
note_en: The lengths are nearly the same, but Hewitt plays the first refrain once more. Sokolov carries the second half at nearly the maximum, while Hewitt plays loudest, then keeps the ending soft.

title_en: Maisky Sinks Deep, Yo-Yo Ma Rises Evenly
note_en: Maisky is 11 seconds longer. Maisky sinks deeply once in the early part and once in the later part, while Yo-Yo Ma builds step by step without much reduction.

title_en: Even Schiff, Softly Building Hewitt
note_en: Hewitt is 14 seconds longer. Schiff keeps an even level from the opening, while Hewitt opens very softly and builds step by step for over a minute.

title_en: Lim Takes a Long Breath, Perahia Goes Straight On
note_en: Lim is 34 seconds longer. Before the end, Lim goes very soft for nearly 10 seconds, while Perahia lowers the level briefly and goes straight on.

title_en: Domingo Steps Up, Carreras Loud Early
note_en: Carreras sings the first climax at nearly the final level. Domingo keeps the first climax much lower and raises the level a step with each climax.

title_en: Gardiner Loud on Two Lines, Harnoncourt Raises Each Line
note_en: Harnoncourt raises the level each time the chorus enters. Gardiner is mostly soft and rises loudly only in the middle two lines, and runs about 10 seconds shorter.

title_en: Chung Rises Early, Kremer Holds the Hush Long
note_en: Chung is 33 seconds shorter. Chung ends the soft introduction at about 25 seconds and rises loudly, while Kremer keeps it soft for over 40 seconds before getting louder.

title_en: Solti Sinks Deep, Rattle Rises Early
note_en: In the quiet passage in the middle, Solti sinks very deeply and Rattle less. Afterward Rattle reaches nearly the maximum right away, while Solti holds back for about a minute longer.

title_en: Heinrich Schiff Loud for Long, Kanneh-Mason Deeply Soft
note_en: Heinrich Schiff stays loud for over 18 seconds from the first chord, and the quiet spot in the middle is shallow. Kanneh-Mason's quiet spot is much deeper.

title_en: Solti Opens Loud, Dudamel Sustains to the End
note_en: Solti opens loudly from the strings' first notes and comes down deeply at the end. Dudamel keeps the opening small, sustains the loud passages longer, and closes loudly too.

title_en: Rana Steps Back Often, Pollini Pushes Straight
note_en: Rana is 24 seconds longer. Rana steps back deeply several times within the fast passage, while Pollini passes the same spots shallowly and pushes straight on near the maximum.

title_en: Solti Comes Down Evenly, Karajan Sustains Long
note_en: Karajan is 37 seconds longer. Solti comes down evenly about 15 seconds after the climax, while Karajan stays big for over 30 seconds and rises once more about 30 seconds before the end.

title_en: Muti Sinks Deep, Dutoit Pushes to the End
note_en: Muti lowers the quiet passage in the middle deeper, and Dutoit less. In the last minute, Dutoit pushes at nearly the maximum while Muti stays a step below.

title_en: Shallow Leonskaya, Deep-Sinking Melnikov
note_en: In the D minor passage, Melnikov sinks very deeply while Leonskaya passes through far more shallowly. Leonskaya also carries the closing passage on louder.

title_en: Zimerman Holds Back Till the End, Pollini Bursts Early
note_en: Pollini already plays loudest in the loud passage of the early theme and pushes the closing passage just as far. Zimerman raises each loud passage a step and puts the loudest sound at the end.

title_en: Relaxed Son, Yundi Li Gathers at the End
note_en: Son is 26 seconds longer and raises the level from the early big passage to nearly the final level. Yundi Li keeps the early part low and raises it all at once in the last big passage.

title_en: Argerich Builds Early, Cho Holds Back to the End
note_en: Argerich is 18 seconds shorter and already raises the level close to the maximum in the middle of the quiet march. Cho walks low for over a minute and raises it only at the loud chords.

title_en: Shelley Sinks Deep, Hough Stays Even
note_en: Shelley is 39 seconds shorter and sinks the quiet passage after the climax very deeply. Hough doesn't sink deeply even in quiet passages and carries on at an even level.

title_en: Ashkenazy Strong at the Start, Pollini Strong at the Back
note_en: Ashkenazy gets nearly to the maximum 4 seconds in. Pollini pushes at an even level for over a minute and rises to nearly the maximum only in the later part.

title_en: Pires Peaks Late, Lisiecki Peaks at the Opening
note_en: Lisiecki is already loudest at the opening chord, where the winds break in forcefully. Pires holds back a step there and gets nearly to the maximum only as 4 minutes approach.

title_en: Marriner Rises Sparingly, Zinman Builds from the Front
note_en: Zinman is 1:10 longer. Marriner keeps the early ascent low and raises it all at once from a minute before the climax, while Zinman builds loudly from the start.

title_en: Marriner Lowers Early, Bernstein Lowers Late and Deep
note_en: Marriner already lowers to a soft level when the theme is repeated. Bernstein pushes loudly through that theme, then sinks much deeper at the oboe passage.

title_en: Harnoncourt Often Loud, Böhm Only Briefly
note_en: Harnoncourt is 53 seconds shorter. Harnoncourt often rises close to the maximum, while Böhm presses the middle down low and keeps the loud places brief.

title_en: Bernstein Holds Back, Nézet-Séguin Raises Early
note_en: Bernstein doesn't raise the level until before the last big passage, then holds that passage near the maximum for almost 30 seconds. Nézet-Séguin raises it loudly even in the middle and climbs the ending in two stages.

title_en: Gardiner Filling, Leonhardt Growing
note_en: Gardiner enters loudly from the start and fills the sound at nearly the same level to the end. Leonhardt opens softly, builds little by little up to the exact middle, then sets it down again.

title_en: Slow Fischer-Dieskau, Goerne Ending Softly
note_en: Goerne is 1:22 shorter. Fischer-Dieskau keeps a similar level to the end, while Goerne lowers the last minute a step and ends softly.

title_en: Ashkenazy Rises Early, Lim Presses Deep
note_en: Lim is 10 seconds shorter. Ashkenazy plays loudest in the early part, while Lim sinks the middle deeply and plays loudest after it.

title_en: Even Tilling, Slow and Soft Hendricks
note_en: Hendricks is 1:06 longer. Tilling has fewer and shallower quiet passages; Hendricks drops more often and deeper.

title_en: Slow, Deep Mutter, Even Perlman
note_en: Mutter is 34 seconds longer. Mutter sinks deeply after the climax, while Perlman reaches the maximum at the early high point and keeps the quiet passages shallow.

title_en: Bernstein in Two Steps, Dutoit in One
note_en: Dutoit keeps a soft level until 30 seconds before the end, then rises loudly in one go. Bernstein rises in two steps from before that.

title_en: Long Bartoli, Deep-Lowering Berganza
note_en: Bartoli is 23 seconds longer. Bartoli rises to near the maximum several times near the end, while Berganza sinks deeply right after the loudest singing.

title_en: Ashkenazy Builds Slowly, Lupu Rises Early
note_en: Ashkenazy is 10 seconds longer. Ashkenazy reaches nearly the maximum only at the end, while Lupu is already near the maximum about two-thirds of the way through.

title_en: Lang Lang Grows the Ending, Argerich Ends Softly
note_en: Lang Lang carries the theme at an even level, then raises it loudly again in the last phrase. Argerich rises loudly in the middle and ends the last phrase softly.

title_en: Perlman Big Three Times, Janssen Loudest at the Last Chord
note_en: Perlman plays the two tuttis and the last chord at nearly the same level. Janssen keeps the tuttis lower, and the loudest sound comes on the last chord.

title_en: Boulez Loud Early, Bernstein Loud Only at the End
note_en: Boulez rises to the loudest level less than a minute after the alto enters. Bernstein reaches that level only 10 seconds before the end.

title_en: Konwitschny at the First Rush, Haitink at the Second
note_en: Konwitschny already rises to the loudest level at the first onrush. Haitink holds back the first onrush for a long time, passes through a deeply soft middle, and bursts out at the second.

title_en: Abbado on the First Chord, Karajan Long and Loud
note_en: Karajan is 1:21 longer. Abbado rings out the first chord loudest and presses the middle low, while Karajan rises to nearly the maximum several times even in the middle dialogue.

title_en: Karajan Opens Softly, Bernstein Drags Slowly
note_en: Bernstein is 21 seconds longer, and most of the difference arises in the first 1:30. Karajan's opening is very soft, while Bernstein swells conspicuously once within 14 seconds of the start.

title_en: Solti Big from the Start, Abbado Builds
note_en: Solti plays near the maximum from the opening and is loudest at the first ff. Abbado keeps the first f a step lower and builds, reaching the loudest level at the second peak.

title_en: Bernstein's Loud Trumpet, Levine's Lower One
note_en: Bernstein's trumpet signal is nearly as loud as the loud passage of the prayer melody, while Levine's is a step lower. Levine runs 12 seconds longer, and the loudest sound comes in the latter part of the melody.

title_en: Thielemann Strikes Briefly, Chailly Sustains
note_en: Chailly is 21 seconds longer. At the peak where the horns surge, Thielemann hits the maximum briefly and comes down, while Chailly holds a loud level for nearly 15 seconds and reaches the maximum twice.

title_en: Herman Closes Briefly, Thunemann Closes Long
note_en: The two reach the last tutti at almost the same time. Herman finishes that tutti in 12 seconds, while Thunemann carries it on for over 30 seconds.

title_en: Short Introduction with Mutter, Long with Perlman
note_en: Perlman spends 27 seconds longer on the introduction. Perlman's biggest peak in the introduction is loud, close to the Presto, while Mutter's is a step below it.

title_en: Narrow Rise from Zimerman, Wide Rise from Rubinstein
note_en: In the Rubinstein version, the orchestral crescendo starts far lower and rises widely to ff. In the Zimerman version, the first signal already rings loudly, so the range of the rise is narrow.

title_en: Perahia Deep in Quiet Spots, Even Eschenbach
note_en: Perahia's quiet passages are far deeper than Eschenbach's. Eschenbach is 27 seconds shorter and reaches nearly the maximum in every loud passage.

title_en: Kissin Loud from the Start, Firkušný Holds Back
note_en: Kissin rings out at nearly the maximum from the first unison and returns to that level several times. Firkušný reaches nearly the maximum for the first time only a few seconds before the end.

title_en: Deep-Sinking Rozhdestvensky, Even Tjeknavorian
note_en: Tjeknavorian is 44 seconds shorter. Rozhdestvensky sinks deeply between the loud passages and raises the level again, while Tjeknavorian keeps the big level even.

title_en: Shallow Gielen, Deep Nott
note_en: In the quiet passage in the middle, Nott goes very deep and Gielen less. Gielen reaches nearly the maximum only at the last climax.

title_en: Mead Loud Early, Lesne Soft at the Opening
note_en: Mead rises to nearly the maximum in 45 seconds and reaches that level several times. Lesne's opening is very soft, and nearly the maximum appears only twice.

title_en: Kermes Holds Back, Crowe Raises Often
note_en: The two performances differ by 1 second in length. Kermes reaches nearly the maximum only once and goes deep in the quiet places, while Crowe reaches nearly the maximum four times in the second half.

title_en: Fast Harnoncourt, Less Soft Bernstein
note_en: Bernstein is 5 seconds longer. After the two chords, Harnoncourt plays the cello theme very softly and Bernstein less softly.

title_en: Shallow Latvian Radio Choir, Deep Weinberg
note_en: The Latvian Radio Choir is less soft even in the later quiet passage and reaches nearly the maximum from the first section. Weinberg goes deep in the later quiet passage, and the first section is a step lower.

title_en: Capuçon Deep in the Middle, Batiashvili Shallow
note_en: In the middle quiet passage, Capuçon stays very soft for over 40 seconds. Batiashvili's quiet middle is short and shallow, so the difference in level is small.

title_en: Bernstein Bursts at Once, Dutoit Builds at the End
note_en: Bernstein reaches nearly the maximum as soon as the racing passage starts and sustains it for nearly 20 seconds. Dutoit drags the same passage a step lower and raises it to the loudest only in the last few seconds.

title_en: Galante Sinks Long, Fleming Passes Quickly
note_en: After the early big passage, Galante draws out the quiet passage deeply for nearly 30 seconds. Fleming passes through the quiet passage after the big one in about 20 seconds, less softly, and the aria is over 20 seconds shorter.

title_en: Paik Max at Once, Pires Held Back to the End
note_en: Paik already plays loudest at the first peak and releases the diminished seventh chord early. Pires keeps the first two peaks a step lower, plays loudest on that chord, and lets it ring for a long time.

title_en: Böhm Rises Early, Haitink Arrives Only at the End
note_en: Böhm is 19 seconds shorter than Haitink and already rises near the maximum at the second motif. Haitink leaves long gaps between motifs and reaches the maximum only near the final chord.
